label: prf:torus-embeddable-complete
title: Proof of torus embeddable complete
html:
Proof. The Seifert genus of T_{m,n} is g(T_{m,n}) = (m-1)(n-1)/2. Embeddability requires g(T_{m,n}) \leq g(\Sigma_4) = 4, i.e., (m-1)(n-1) \leq 8. We enumerate all coprime pairs (m,n) with 1 < m < n satisfying this bound:

  • m = 2: (2-1)(n-1) = n-1 \leq 8, so n \leq 9. Odd coprime values: n \in \{3, 5, 7, 9\}.

  • m = 3: (3-1)(n-1) = 2(n-1) \leq 8, so n \leq 5. Coprime to 3: n \in \{4, 5\}.

  • m = 4: (4-1)(n-1) = 3(n-1) \leq 8, so n \leq 3. But m < n requires n \geq 5; no solution.

  • m \geq 5: (m-1)(n-1) \geq 4 \cdot m > 8 for n > m \geq 5; no solution.

This exhausts all cases. The six nontrivial torus knots listed above, together with the unknot, form the complete set of torus knots embeddable in \Sigma_4. No torus knot outside \mathcal{G} admits a localized knot structure in the Descartes universe. \square
